accused_victim_relationship: Prior dispute: alleged property dispute between the victim and his son Prem Singh (not an appellant); the appellants' relationship to the victim is not stated
weapon: Rusted iron rod (recovered at instance of Kamal Kishore); sweater alleged to have been used for strangulation
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last seen witnesses, Call Detail Records, identification, recoveries)
aggravating_circumstances: None noted (prosecution alleged earlier beatings and threats by the son; not accepted by the Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; rigorous imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.50,000 each
high_court_outcome: Appeals dismissed; conviction and life sentence affirmed
neutral_facts: On 10 September 2009, at about 4:15 pm, the victim's brother went to the victim's house and found the victim lying dead on a cot. The victim's elder brother also reached the spot, and the victim was taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. The First Information Report was lodged expressing suspicion against the victim's son, who had a property dispute with the victim and was alleged to have earlier beaten and threatened the victim. The son fled the scene and was apprehended on 12 September 2009. During interrogation, the son allegedly named two associates, the accused. On the instance of one accused, a rusted iron rod was recovered. On the instance of the other accused, a sweater was recovered, which was alleged to have been used to strangle the victim. A witness stated that on the day of the incident, at about 3:15 pm, he saw the victim's son in a vehicle in front of the victim's room, pressing the accelerator loudly, and saw two boys come out of the room, whom the son described as tenants. This witness and the victim's younger brother gave similar accounts. The witness stated that he first saw the accused at the police station on 12 September 2009, where the police had already shown them to him, and the identification parade was refused. Call detail records of mobile numbers allegedly used by the accused were said to place their location at the scene. One of the numbers was registered in another person's name, and no evidence showed how the SIM came into the accused's possession.
physical_harm: Death of the victim (prosecution alleged strangulation)
motive: alleged: property dispute between the victim and his son
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted; the Court found the last seen evidence, identification and CDR evidence unreliable
witness_credibility: PW-20 (younger brother): presence doubtful, substantial improvement from his Section 161 statement. PW-21: declared hostile, first saw the accused at the police station. Both found unreliable.
post_offence_conduct: Alleged: the victim's son fled the scene and was apprehended on 12 September 2009; not accepted as proof against the accused
bail_history: Bail bonds of the appellants to be discharged; grant and duration of bail otherwise not stated
trial_duration: offence: 10 September 2009; trial judgment: 17 May 2013; High Court: 5 August 2014; Supreme Court: 7 August 2023
legal_representation: Appellants: Mrs. K. Sarada Devi, Ms. Kheyali Singh, R K Kapoor and others. State: Ms. Sonia Mathur, Sr. Adv., A.K. Panda and others for the respondent.
investigation_status: FIR registered; suspects apprehended; charge-sheet filed; case committed to the Sessions Judge
procedural_irregularity: Accused were shown to witnesses at the police station before the test identification parade, which made the parade's sanctity doubtful
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted s.302 r/w s.34 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, convictions quashed, acquitted.
prosecution_argument: Concurrent findings of the trial court and High Court on proper appreciation of evidence; no interference warranted
defence_argument: Circumstantial case requires an unbroken chain of circumstances; the prosecution relied on the testimony of PW-20 and PW-21, which was unreliable
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence test (five conditions from Sharad Birdhichand Sarda): circumstances fully established, consistent only with guilt, complete chain excluding innocence; suspicion cannot replace proof beyond reasonable doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116 : [1985] 1 SCR 88
other_sentence_order: Appellants to be set at liberty if not required in any other case; bail bonds discharged
